recommendation.paragraph: Recent sales of similar homes in Tanager Ridge, adjusted for their differences from yours, point to a value of about {low} to {high}, a narrow range because four of the five agree closely. We recommend launching at {list_price}, just above the median adjusted sale of about {median_adjusted} and just under the $390,000 search line many buyers use. It leaves room for the negotiating that is normal now and presents the home as fairly priced in its first weeks, when buyer attention is highest. A home with your floor plan on your street, 853 Tanager Ridge Dr, asked $419,900 and expired after 121 days, and the only sale near $405,000 had both baths remodeled and sold in June, when the market was stronger.

means: Expect to negotiate. Homes nearby that sold since {split_month} closed at about {sale_to_list_recent} of their original asking price after seller-paid costs, and most sellers paid part of the buyer's closing costs, typically about {credit_amount_recent}.

The first three weeks matter most. A new listing gets its biggest wave of showings right away. Priced where buyers expect, that wave turns into offers; priced high, the home sits and the price cut comes later, from a weaker position.

Watch the appraisal. The highest similar non-pool sale nearby since April was $412,500, a fully updated home with impact windows that sold in May. A contract well above {high} would risk a low appraisal and a renegotiation.

Documentation is worth money. The permitted roof and AC are among the most valuable facts in the listing, because roof age decides whether a buyer can insure the home. Have the permits and final inspections ready on day one.

comps.intro: We looked at every sale within about a mile since April 2026 and chose the five closest matches: three-bedroom, two-bath homes in Tanager Ridge of about 1,540 to 1,660 square feet, built in the mid-1980s, without a pool. Each is adjusted for its differences from your home, so it reflects what that home would have sold for if it were yours.
comps.method_note: Adjustments used: about $75 per square foot of size difference; $10,000 where a comp had an updated kitchen but original baths (your hall bath and newer roof give you a small edge); $10,000 off a comp with both baths remodeled; $25,000 for a home with an original kitchen and baths; about {time_rate} per quarter off sales from before {time_cutoff}, because prices have softened since spring. Seller-paid costs are subtracted from the sale price, since they reduce what the seller actually received. Condition adjustments are based on listing descriptions, not visits, so they are judgment calls.

prep.intro: These steps cost little and remove the questions that slow Florida buyers down or cost sellers money at the negotiating table.
items: Document the roof and AC. Have the 2021 roof permit and final inspection and the 2023 AC permit ready to share. Roof age decides whether a buyer can insure the home, so a documented 2021 roof is one of the most valuable facts in the listing.
Get a 4-point and wind-mitigation report. Buyers can get insurance quotes before they offer. With original single-pane windows, the wind-mitigation report shows exactly what credits the roof earns.
Gather the kitchen records. The electrical permit plus invoices for the cabinets, counters and appliances. Records turn the 2024 remodel from a claim into value an appraiser can rely on.
Consider a pre-listing inspection. You learn about any issue before a buyer uses it to renegotiate.
Decide on a seller-credit budget now. Most recent sales included one. A credit toward a rate buydown lowers a buyer's payment more in the first years than the same amount off the price.
Agree on a review point. If there are steady showings but no offer after about three weeks, we revisit the price with fresh data rather than waiting.

needs: Copies of the 2021 roof permit and final inspection, and the 2023 AC permit.
The kitchen's electrical permit and invoices for the cabinets, counters and appliances.
The lender's payoff letter, to replace your estimate of about $171,500.
Any storm shutters or other wind-protection features, since the windows are original.
Your answers for Florida's flood disclosure: any flood damage, flood insurance claims or flood assistance while you've owned the home.
Anything else you know that affects the home's value or condition. Florida law requires sellers to disclose known material defects.
Confirmation of the December 18 closing target and your move-out timing, so we can plan showings.
method: This analysis uses the property details and updates you described on September 24, 2026; the Seminole County property appraiser's record and 2025 tax bill; a Stellar MLS search of single-family homes within about a mile (sales from April 10 to September 19, 2026, plus current active, pending, expired and canceled listings); and the Freddie Mac weekly mortgage rate survey for September 24, 2026. Florida documentary stamp tax and owner's title insurance are calculated at the state's standard rates.

This is a broker's opinion of value based on comparable sales. It is not an appraisal. Expected sale prices, timelines, costs and net proceeds are estimates for planning, not guarantees; your closing agent will provide exact figures. Condition adjustments are based on listing descriptions of the comparable homes and on the updates you described, and will be refined once we see your records. Market conditions change, so this analysis should be refreshed if the home is not listed within a few weeks.
